scope_contract: Every Azure CLI query must include the explicitly authorized subscription and/or exact resource ID. Do not change the default subscription, acquire credentials, or run mutation commands as part of diagnosis.

diagnostics.purpose: Separate client resolver results from Azure Private DNS zone, link, and record configuration.
commands: az network private-dns record-set a list --resource-group <resource_group> --zone-name <private_dns_zone> --subscription <subscription_id> --output json
diagnostics.interpretation: Compare the client answer with the intended private record and verify the client VNet uses a resolver that can reach the linked zone. DNS success does not prove TCP reachability.
diagnostics.verification: Local tool has DNS probe tests; no Azure DNS query was run.

diagnostics.purpose: Inspect the NIC's effective routes for the target prefix and next hop.
diagnostics.interpretation: Compare the longest matching prefix, next-hop type, and next-hop address against the intended path; an effective route is not an end-to-end connectivity test.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; Azure route query not run.

diagnostics.purpose: Resolve a target and test direct TCP connectivity plus an optional certificate-verified TLS handshake.
diagnostics.interpretation: The probe reports DNS, TCP, certificate validation, negotiated TLS version, and certificate fingerprint; it sends no application payload.
diagnostics.verification: Local loopback tests only; no external network probe was run.

diagnostics.purpose: Read the effective NSG set attached to a specific NIC.
diagnostics.interpretation: Evaluate priority, direction, protocol, source/destination prefix, and port against the actual five-tuple. Effective rules do not prove a remote service is listening.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; Azure NSG query not run.

diagnostics.purpose: Inspect the exact Private Endpoint and its DNS zone-group association.
commands: az network private-endpoint dns-zone-group list --resource-group <resource_group> --endpoint-name <private_endpoint_name> --subscription <subscription_id> --output json
diagnostics.interpretation: Check provisioning/connection state, target resource, NIC private IP, zone group and client-side DNS answer separately. A healthy endpoint does not prove client DNS or route reachability.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; Azure Private Endpoint query not run.

diagnostics.purpose: Inspect only the identity attachment on one explicitly named Azure resource.
diagnostics.interpretation: Compare principal/client/tenant identifiers and identity type with the workload's expected identity. An attached identity does not prove token acquisition or target authorization.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; Azure identity query not run.

diagnostics.purpose: Inspect only allowlisted JWT claims locally without printing the token.
diagnostics.interpretation: The tool reports aud, selected issuer/tenant and lifetime claims but does not verify the signature, issuer, tenant, token type or authorization. Supply the token through hidden interactive input; never put it in argv or logs.
diagnostics.verification: Synthetic JWT claim tests only; no token acquired or inspected.

diagnostics.purpose: List direct and inherited role assignments for one exact resource scope.
commands: az role assignment list --scope <scope_resource_id> --include-inherited --all --fill-principal-name false --fill-role-definition-name false --subscription <subscription_id> --output json
diagnostics.interpretation: Compare the caller principal, role definition, assignment scope, condition and inheritance with the required operation. A role assignment listing may be incomplete if the operator lacks read access.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; Azure RBAC query not run.

diagnostics.purpose: Inspect one vault's RBAC/network configuration and, only when explicitly approved, test metadata-list access without reading secret values.
commands: az keyvault secret list --vault-name <approved_probe_vault> --subscription <subscription_id> --maxresults 1 --query '[].{id:id, enabled:attributes.enabled}' --output json
diagnostics.interpretation: Separate control-plane configuration from data-plane authorization and network reachability. The optional list operation returns metadata only, but still requires explicit owner approval because secret names are sensitive metadata.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; no vault was queried and no secret was accessed.

diagnostics.purpose: Read the latest Policy compliance state for one resource and its scoped assignments.
diagnostics.interpretation: Check assignment scope/exclusions, definition/effect, evaluation timestamp and resource state; compliance state can lag a recent change and is not itself a deployment error payload.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; Azure Policy query not run.

diagnostics.purpose: Inspect pod waiting states and warning events in an explicitly selected Kubernetes context and namespace.
diagnostics.interpretation: Look for ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff, event reason/message, image reference, service account and registry authorization path. Do not query Secret objects or print pull credentials.
diagnostics.verification: Documented only; no Kubernetes context/cluster was available for this check.

diagnostics.purpose: Probe a specific unauthenticated HTTP(S) health endpoint using HEAD without reading a response body or following redirects.
diagnostics.interpretation: Record status and latency; confirm the service's health endpoint supports HEAD and compare with the service's own availability contract. This is not a business transaction test.
diagnostics.verification: Local loopback HTTP test only; no application endpoint was contacted.

diagnostics.purpose: Read a named platform metric for one resource and use the prepared KQL files only in a workspace with confirmed schema and query permission.
commands: az monitor metrics list --resource <resource_id> --metrics <metric_name> --interval PT5M --aggregation Average --subscription <subscription_id> --output json
diagnostics.interpretation: Preserve metric namespace, aggregation, interval, time range, dimensions, and absence of data separately. KQL files are workspace-schema dependent and have not been executed.
diagnostics.verification: Source-documented only; no metric or Log Analytics query was run.

global_limits: Read-only diagnostic commands can still reveal resource names, network topology, principal IDs, or secret names; store outputs as sensitive operational evidence.
Never treat an empty response as proof that an object does not exist until scope, permission, query time range, and data source are confirmed.
No catalog entry authenticates, changes the default subscription, registers a provider, changes Azure resources, or authorizes a live experiment.
